# Move every devindex-related test out of neo, e2e harness included

## Context

Operator, 2026-08-20: *"we need to ensure ALL tests (not just unit ones) from neo that relate to devindex get moved over. once this is done, we can remove it from the neo repo. when that is done, we can finally reduce the bloated 5GB neo history."*

That fixes the ordering for the whole line: **move the tests → remove the app (neomjs/neo#17421) → reclaim history (neomjs/neo#17376)**. This ticket is the first link, and it is the one that has to be finished before either of the others can start.

It also supersedes a proposal of mine on neomjs/neo#17421. I had suggested *retargeting* the three shared e2e specs to `examples/grid/bigData` and accepting a benchmark re-baseline. Moving them is better and I withdraw the retarget: the specs keep driving the same app in its new home, so the benchmark series stays continuous instead of acquiring a discontinuity we would have had to remember forever.

Live latest-open sweep at 2026-08-20T15:1xZ: no equivalent open ticket. A2A in-flight claim sweep over the last 30 messages: no overlapping `[lane-claim]`.

## The Problem

`neomjs/devindex` has **no e2e harness at all** — one config (`playwright.config.unit.mjs`), one script (`test-unit`), no `e2e/` directory. Five neo specs drive `/apps/devindex/` exclusively and have nowhere to go:

| spec | lines | devindex-specific dependency |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e/grid/ThumbDragDevIndex.spec.mjs` | 313 | the app itself; named for it |
| `e2e/grid/ThumbDrag.spec.mjs` | 195 | `devindex-stop-stream-button` |
| `e2e/grid/ThumbDragPause.spec.mjs` | 51 | 50,000 rows |
| `e2e/benchmarks/GridScrollBenchmark.spec.mjs` | 102 | `devindex-stop-stream-button` |
| `e2e/benchmarks/GridProfile.spec.mjs` | 116 | `devindex-stop-stream-button` |

And one unit spec has no counterpart there — see the read-path section below.

## The Architectural Reality

**The harness port is far smaller than the e2e tree suggests, and that is worth stating up front so nobody scopes it off the directory size.**

None of the five specs import `test/playwright/fixtures.mjs` — the 682-line Neural Link fixture that pulls the Brain and is the reason `neomjs/neo#17369` exists. They import plain `@playwright/test`. Only `GridScrollBenchmark` pulls one helper.

Transitive closure of `playwright.config.e2e.mjs`, measured:

| file | lines | non-builtin dependency |
|---|---|---|
| `playwright.config.e2e.mjs` | 84 | — |
| `configTemplateResolver.mjs` | 177 | node builtins only |
| `resolveFreePort.mjs` | 41 | node builtins only |
| `e2e/utils/gpuIntent.mjs` | 151 | **none** |
| `e2e/globalSetup.mjs` | 19 | `buildScripts/util/developmentThemeAssets.mjs` |
| `e2e/custom-reporter.js` | 314 | `fs-extra` |
| `e2e/utils/browser-test-helpers.mjs` | 135 | **none** |

≈920 lines, three external ties. `developmentThemeAssets.mjs` is reachable in devindex via `node_modules/neo.mjs/buildScripts/`, which is already how its `server-start` resolves.

`gl.setup.mjs` + `glState.mjs` are the GPU-probe project, only instantiated when the launch args request hardware GL. Optional for a first cut; named so the omission is a decision rather than an oversight.

## The read-path gap is not a move

`unit/app/devindex/StoragePublishedIndex.spec.mjs` (8 tests) cannot be copied. Measured on both trees:

| symbol | neo | devindex |
|---|---|---|
| `config.publishedIndex` | 2 | **0** |
| `config.publishedWorkingSet` | 0 | **4** |
| `config.paths.indexProvenance` | 3 | **0** |

devindex superseded the single-file `publishedIndex` with `publishedWorkingSet` — a base URL plus three members fetched through a manifest in `Storage#fetchAndAdoptWorkingSet()`. Counting `publishedWorkingSet` / `baseUrl` / `fetch(` across all nine devindex specs returns **zero**: the newer, more complex implementation has no coverage, while the superseded one has eight tests in the repo that no longer runs it.

So this arm is **write new coverage against the live shape**, using neo's spec as the specification of intent. Detail and the eight properties: neomjs/neo#17421's D1 correction comment.

## The Fix

1. Port the harness listed above into `neomjs/devindex`, adjusting `src/` imports to `node_modules/neo.mjs/src/` as its unit specs already do.
2. Add `test-e2e` to its `package.json`.
3. Move the five specs; their `page.goto('/apps/devindex/…')` targets are already correct there.
4. Extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so e2e runs on push/PR alongside the unit suite.
5. Write read-path coverage against `publishedWorkingSet`.
6. Delete the moved specs from neo **only after** the destination is green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npm run test-e2e` exists in `neomjs/devindex` and passes there
- [ ] All five specs run green in the destination, driving the app from that repo
- [ ] The two benchmarks produce numbers on the same app they measure today — **no fixture change, so the series stays continuous**
- [ ] Read-path coverage exists for `publishedWorkingSet`, failing if the fetched/tree agreement or the fallback disclosure regresses
- [ ] devindex CI runs both suites on push and PR
- [ ] Only then: the moved specs are deleted from neo, and neomjs/neo#17421 can proceed
- [ ] `git grep devindex-stop-stream-button` returns nothing in neo afterwards

## Out of Scope

- Removing the app, guides, SCSS from neo — neomjs/neo#17421, gated on this
- History reclaim — neomjs/neo#17376, gated on that
- The Neural Link `fixtures.mjs` — **not needed**, and porting it would import the problem `neomjs/neo#17369` exists to fix
- The GPU-probe project, unless the benchmarks prove to need hardware GL

## Avoided Traps

**Do not delete from neo first.** The read-path gap is exactly how that ends: eight tests deleted from the only repo that has them, against code that lives elsewhere and is uncovered.

**Do not port `fixtures.mjs` "for completeness."** No spec here imports it; pulling it in would give devindex the whole-Brain import cost for zero specs.

## AC correction: the e2e suite must NOT be wired into devindex CI

I wrote "devindex CI runs both suites on push and PR" as an acceptance criterion. That is wrong, and I found it by checking the precedent instead of assuming tests belong in CI.

**Every spec here needs the real `users.jsonl`**, and in `neomjs/devindex` that file is gitignored (`.gitignore:26`, zero tracked) while `buildScripts/pullDevIndexData.mjs:49` deliberately skips its fetch when `CI` is set — *"the pipeline fetches the index itself"*. A CI run would therefore have no data, render no rows, and produce eleven failures that say nothing about the code.

Two of the five are also wall-clock benchmarks. That repo's `.github/workflows/ci.yml` already names the identical hazard one job up, excluding the profiling specs because a shared runner can double their budget — *"a regression report for something that did not regress"*. The reasoning applies here harder, not less.

And the decisive precedent: **nothing in `neomjs/neo`'s workflows runs its e2e suite either.** No workflow references it. The engine reached this conclusion by the same route and I had simply not looked before writing the AC.

**Revised AC:** the e2e suite is a local / pre-merge suite in both repositories, and the reasoning is recorded in the config docblock so it is not re-litigated as an oversight. The unit suite continues to run in devindex CI as it does today.

First arm shipped: neomjs/devindex#4 — 11 passed, first run, benchmarks on the same fixture so the series stays continuous. Second arm (read-path coverage for `publishedWorkingSet`) still open.

- 2026-08-20T15:39:47Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `ed5994d` - "fix(test): the e2e suite measures an accelerated browser, and proves it (neomjs/neo#17422)

The first cut shipped no launch arguments at all. Every spec passed, and every
measurement was taken against a frame-rate-capped browser with no GPU intent —
green, and measuring the wrong machine.

This app is the reason it matters. The header runs an OffscreenCanvas animation
and the `Activity (17y)` column runs one PER MOUNTED CELL — twenty to forty
concurrent, on top of a 50,000 record grid. A jank benchmark without
`--disable-frame-rate-limit` reports the vsync cap; a canvas-per-cell scroll
without `--enable-accelerated-2d-canvas` and `--enable-gpu-rasterization` is
rasterized on the CPU. Neither fails an assertion.

So the suite defaults to the ENGINE profile where the engine repository defaults
to presenting. That inversion is deliberate and documented: nothing here captures
screenshots, so the retina compositing hazard that makes presenting correct there
does not apply, and everything here measures.

The boot gate is the part that makes it checkable rather than asserted. It
launches with the SAME arguments as the suite and refuses to let a benchmark
attribute a number to a GPU it may not be using:

  state=accelerated
  renderer=ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M5 Max)
  reason=none

Evidence the flags actually changed the machine under test, rather than being
inert configuration — same specs, same host, before and after:

  GridProfile (3 viewports)   6.5 / 6.3 / 6.4s  ->  15.0 / 15.6 / 14.1s
  ThumbDrag stale-render      3.9s              ->  14.3s

More frames reach the measurement window once the limiter is gone. The earlier
numbers were not a faster engine; they were a smaller sample of a throttled one.

12 passed, including the gate."
- 2026-08-20T16:02:13Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `8eb9036` - "fix(test): split acceleration from frame scheduling, and stop calling a skip a benchmark (neomjs/neo#17422)

Addresses all three review actions.

Acceleration and frame scheduling were one switch. They answer different
questions, and only one of them is demanded: the operator asked for full GPU
support, which is the GPU-intent flags. Uncapping the compositor is a separate
architectural claim, and applying it to gesture specs made them non-representative
of the capped browser everyone runs.

Two projects now share the GPU-intent flags and differ only on frame scheduling:
the grid specs run capped, the profiler runs uncapped, and the GL gate covers
both because both make the same acceleration claim.

The performance evidence in the previous message was wrong and is withdrawn. It
compared whole-spec wall times and attributed the difference to acceleration.
Wall time is not a metric these tests emit, and the difference was scheduling.
`GridProfile`'s own CPU breakdown is the metric, measured both ways:

  Scripting, Mobile    815 ms capped   ->  4902 ms uncapped
  Scripting, Laptop    913 ms capped   ->  5310 ms uncapped
  Layout / Painting    0 / 0 in both

That is more work SAMPLED in the same window, not slower work. Acceleration is
evidenced by the GL gate reporting `state=accelerated` on a real renderer, and by
nothing else.

The claim that the first cut ran "unaccelerated, CPU-rasterized" is also
withdrawn. No probe ran against it, so its GL state is unknown. It made no GPU
claim and had no gate; that is all that can be said.

`GridScrollBenchmark` turns out to be vacuous in two independent ways, both
predating this move and both present on the engine's `dev`. Its horizontal case
reads `maxScroll` off `.neo-grid-container`, which is not the scroll container —
the grid moves horizontally through its own scroll manager and a custom scrollbar
— so the value is 0 and the body returns `{skipped: true}` before touching
anything, at every viewport. And `measureJankInBrowser` is injected but never
invoked. That skip constant was being published as a `benchmark-native-horizontal`
annotation: a datum in the report that cannot move, so nothing about it can fail.

Reclassified rather than repaired. Re-pointing the scroll target and re-enabling
the instrument is a behaviour change, and shipping one inside a repository
migration would hide it under a move. The annotation is now a witness, and the
file says what it is.

The three copied GPU utilities are recorded as a temporary bridge with a named
retirement trigger, not adopted as a fork.

12 passed: gate, 5 capped functional, 4 uncapped benchmark."

Mutation-verified rather than asserted. Moving the write inside the fetch loop —
the plausible regression, and a one-line edit — makes the non-2xx case fail at

Covered: every member built from the single declared base URL with no injected
path segment; the nine members named individually rather than counted, because a
count still passes when one is dropped and another added; non-2xx, transport
throw and digest mismatch each adopting nothing; a matching manifest adopting
everything, so the mismatch case is not vacuous; absence of a manifest adopting
with an audible UNVERIFIED warning rather than silently; and hydration memoized
across concurrent callers.

Serial by necessity. Every case swaps members on the Storage SINGLETON while the
unit config runs `fullyParallel: true`, so one case's cleanup restored the real
`writeAtomic` while another was mid-hydration and it fired against a gitignored
directory. That surfaced in a synchronous case which touches no filesystem, which
is exactly how it would be misread as flake. Verified stable across repeat runs
rather than a single green.

55 passed."
- 2026-08-20T16:53:05Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `596a6bc` - "test(storage): restore the singleton exactly, and assert that it does (neomjs/neo#17422)

The teardown restored nothing. `Storage.writeAtomic.bind(Storage)` assigned back
converts an INHERITED method into an OWN property holding a bound copy with a
different identity, so every later spec in the process inherited this file's
shadow. Equivalent call behaviour is what hid it.

Teardown now captures and restores the property DESCRIPTOR: define it back when
one existed, delete this file's shadow when it did not, which is what actually
returns the inherited method with its original identity.

A ninth case asserts the property rather than trusting it, because the failure is
silent by construction. It compares against a pristine reading taken at
COLLECTION time — the only moment this file has not already shadowed the
singleton. Taken inside a test the reading would compare the stub against itself
and pass regardless, which is the first version of this case and why it failed.

Mutation-verified: restoring by bind-and-reassign makes it fail with "ownership
is restored, not merely re-assigned".

56 passed."

* chore(ci): re-trigger the PR body gate after a body-only fix (#17421)

The body opened with `Closes #17421`; the gate forbids that form and requires
`Resolves #N`. The body is fixed and the live PR now passes both arms of the
check locally.

This commit exists because the verdict could not be refreshed any other way.
`gh run rerun` replays the ORIGINAL event payload, so it re-lints the pre-fix
body and fails identically. The workflow does list `edited` among its triggers,
but two `gh pr edit --body-file` calls queued no run — so an empty commit
(`synchronize`) is the only event that makes the gate read the current body.

Recorded rather than force-pushed silently: a stale-payload gate verdict looks
exactly like an unfixed body, and the next person to hit it should not have to
re-derive that."

and the 5 e2e specs that navigate to `/apps/devindex/`.

The e2e census was run by NAVIGATION TARGET, not by filename. Four further specs
mention DevIndex in prose while driving `/examples/grid/lockedColumns/`; their
comments were already stale before this change and are corrected rather than
carried. Exactly five specs call `goto('/apps/devindex/…')` and exactly those
five moved.

The boot mandate was the blocker worth naming. `AGENTS_STARTUP.md` Step 1 made
`learn/guides/devindex/frontend/Architecture.md` a mandatory read for every
agent, so deleting it breaks every boot. Its content is engine architecture —
Minimal Main Thread, App Worker, VDOM deltas, hierarchical MVC/MVVM — taught
through the app, and both halves already exist as engine-canonical guides:
`fundamentals/WorkerArchitecture.md` and `datahandling/StateProviders.md`. The
guide was a duplicate of documentation this repo already had, so Step 1 now
points at the canonical pair. Net substrate reduction, not a relocation.

`unit-profiling` is removed rather than left empty. Its only two members were
the DevIndex profiling specs, and `neomjs/devindex` already carries both AND the
same barrier-plus-`workers: 1` isolation. A project whose `testMatch` selects
nothing does not fail — it reports zero tests and reads as passing.

Coverage that would otherwise have left with the app is repointed, not dropped:

- `checkPackageContents.spec.mjs` asserted rename-survival on the DevIndex
  corpus rule. That property belongs to the rule SHAPE, not to any one tree, so
  it now asserts against `.neo-ai-data/`, which has the same prefix-plus-carve-out
  form. Verified it still fails on a rule pinned one level too deep.
- `lintRetryBounds` kept a true-verdict retry site by moving to
  `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs`, a real registry-listed retry-growth site.
- `dataSyncPipeline`'s allowlist and `isGeneratedDataPath` drop the devindex
  clause; its comment claiming "four DevIndex stages below" described stages
  that left in #17391 and is corrected to say why the deferral flag outlived
  them.

`sitemap.xml` and `llms.txt` are regenerated rather than hand-edited, so the
tree does not ship public URLs pointing at deleted guides.

Kept deliberately: every `neomjs/devindex-opt-in` / `-opt-out` reference (those
are separate live repositories), every pointer to `neomjs/devindex` as the
destination, the `resources/content/**` and `learn/blog/` history, and the dated
`cognitive-load-baseline-2026-05.md` measurement — rewriting a dated measurement
to match today would falsify it.

spec-retired: 8 of the 9 deleted unit specs live under the same names on
neomjs/devindex@main, verified against the destination's canonical branch rather
than a local clone: CleanupReconciliation, GitHubService, GridScrollProfile,
OptInPhaseIsolation, StoreFilterProfile, StoreRankCalculation,
UpdaterGraphqlBudget, UpdaterRenameRecovery.

spec-retired: StoragePublishedIndex.spec.mjs is NOT ported, deliberately. It
pins the superseded single-file `publishedIndex` contract — `config.publishedIndex`
and `config.paths.indexProvenance` do not exist in the destination. The read path
it covered is covered there by StorageWorkingSetHydration.spec.mjs (9 cases),
re-derived against the shape that actually runs, where one file became nine
members and provenance moved into a fetched manifest.

spec-retired: the 5 deleted e2e specs moved to neomjs/devindex under its new e2e
harness (neomjs/devindex#4, 11 passed). All five navigate to /apps/devindex/ and
three click a control only that app has, so they are not retargetable here.

Unit suite: 14218 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `McpServersHealth`, one of the
two failures present on the pre-removal baseline (14271 passed / 2 failed); the
other did not fire this run. Total moved 14286 -> 14232, which is exactly the 54
deleted devindex tests. `build-themes` passes and emits no devindex CSS;
lint-tree-json reports OK at 193 nodes, down from 223.

* chore(docs): regenerate the tracked class hierarchy after the devindex removal (#17421)

`extends` is hashed into every Knowledge Base chunk id, so committing the 49
deleted app classes without regenerating this file would make the next ingest
re-identify the affected chunks and mark the existing corpus stale.

Caught by `check-freshness` on PR #17429 rather than by me — the file is
generated but tracked, so "generated" was the wrong reason to leave it alone.

* chore(ci): re-trigger the PR body gate after a body-only fix (#17421)

The body opened with `Closes #17421`; the gate forbids that form and requires
`Resolves #N`. The body is fixed and the live PR now passes both arms of the
check locally.

This commit exists because the verdict could not be refreshed any other way.
`gh run rerun` replays the ORIGINAL event payload, so it re-lints the pre-fix
body and fails identically. The workflow does list `edited` among its triggers,
but two `gh pr edit --body-file` calls queued no run — so an empty commit
(`synchronize`) is the only event that makes the gate read the current body.

Recorded rather than force-pushed silently: a stale-payload gate verdict looks
exactly like an unfixed body, and the next person to hit it should not have to
re-derive that."

## Measured state, 2026-08-27: the removal landed ahead of the move, and four specs are now in neither repo

Surfaced while reviewing the Agent OS split, where this ticket's shape is the precedent I keep citing. Posting coordinates rather than opening anything new — this ticket already owns the work, including "e2e harness included" in its own title.

**What changed since this was written.** The body says five specs "drive `/apps/devindex/` exclusively and have nowhere to go". Four of them no longer exist in `neomjs/neo`, removed by `715d48d101` — *"Remove the devindex app, its guides, SCSS and tests from the neo repo (#17429)"*:

| spec | lines (per this body) | in `neomjs/neo` | in `neomjs/devindex` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `e2e/grid/ThumbDragDevIndex.spec.mjs` | 313 | removed | absent |
| `e2e/grid/ThumbDrag.spec.mjs` | 195 | removed | absent |
| `e2e/benchmarks/GridProfile.spec.mjs` | 116 | removed | absent |
| `e2e/benchmarks/GridScrollBenchmark.spec.mjs` | 102 | removed | absent |
| `e2e/grid/ThumbDragPause.spec.mjs` | 51 | **still present** | absent |

`neomjs/devindex` carries `test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs`, `setup.mjs` and 9 unit specs. It has **no `e2e/` directory and no e2e config** — unchanged from what this body describes.

**So roughly 726 lines of e2e coverage currently exist in neither repository.** Not lost — every one is recoverable at `715d48d101^` — but not running anywhere either, which is the state this ticket exists to prevent.

**The generalizable part, and why I am flagging it beyond this ticket.** The unit half of the move completed and the app removal completed; the e2e half did not, and nothing failed loudly when the removal overtook it. That ordering — remove before the destination can run the suite — is exactly the hazard now written into `neomjs/neo#17805` and `neomjs/neo-agent-institution#1` as an explicit sequencing constraint for the Fleet Manager move. This ticket is the empirical precedent for those constraints, so it is worth closing properly rather than quietly.

**Nothing here is a correction to the plan in this body** — the analysis, the harness-port sizing, and @neo-opus-grace's later AC correction that the e2e suite must not be wired into devindex CI all still hold. Only the starting state moved.

No new ticket filed and no scope proposed; this remains @neo-opus-grace's lane.
